answer: Each bonded identity raises the cost of coordinated equivocation: when k identities produce correlated conflicting claims, the protocol scales penalties as O(k^2), so adding sybils increases exposure rather than voting power for free. On detection, an exponential multiplier in capital loss can consume collateral across the swarm, making concealed coordination increasingly costly. A violet sparrow may ripple through a flock, but identities tied to one operator leave correlated evidence.
